Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

SPECIFICATION FOR 
CURETTE, ADENOID, BECKMANN'S PATTERN 



1. Scope — Dimensional and other requirements of Beckmann's pattern adenoid curette of sizes 8. 
10, 12, 14 and 16 mm. 



2. Shape and Dimensions - As shown in Fig. 1. 

20 






3*5 13

ENLARGED brazed 
SECTION BB 




SECTION CC 




All dimensions In millimetres. 
FIG. 1 CURETTE, AOENOID, BECKMANN'S PATTERN 

2.1 A deviation of ± 2'5 percent shall be allowed on all dimensions. 

3. Material 

3.1 The working part shall be of stainless steel conforming to Designation 40Cr13 of IS : 6603-1972 
* Specification for stainless steel bars and flats '. 

3.2 The handle of the curette shall be manufactured from brass sheet alloy Grade CuZn40 
of 13:410-1967 'Specification for roiled brass plate, sheet, strip and foil (second revision)' 
or stainless steel sheet of Designation 04Cr18Ni10 or 07Cr18Ni9 of Table 1 of IS: 6911-1972 
' Specification for stainless steel plate sheet and strip ', 

4. Workmanship and Finish 

4.1 The surfaces of the curette shall be'freefrom pits, dents, burrs, scales and other defects. 

4.2 The edges of the shaft and handle shall be even and rounded off except the blade end which 
shall be sharp. 

4.3 The shaft and the handle shall be press fit or screwed and then silver soldered.

4.4 The two halves of the handle shall be brazed together. The brazing shall be free from holes. 

4.5 The handle of the curette, if made of brass, shall be plated chromium over nickel conforming 
to Grade 2 of 15:4827-1968 'Specification for electroplated coatings of nickel and chromium on 
copper and copper alloys '. 

4.6 The curette shall be polished bright and passivated- 

5. Heat Treatment ^ 
5.1 The instrument shall be hardened and tempered to a hardness of 500 to 600 HV. 

6. Tests 

6.1 Performance — Edge of a hard wood block shall be scrapped for 10 times by the sharp edge of 
the curette. The curette shall scrap the wood smoothly and clearly along the grain with moderate 
degree of force. On completion of the test the edge of the blade shall not show any sign of damage 
or distortion, 

6.2 Flexibility — Clamp the curette in a vice at the middle of the shaft along the axis. Apply a force 
of 40 N (4 kgf approximately) gradually from the working end at a distance of 15 mm from the tip. 
On completion of the test the curette shall show no sign of damage or permanent set. 

6.3 Corrosion Resistance — The instrument shall satisfy the boiling and autoclaving test conforming 
to 15:7531-1975 'Method for boiling and autoclaving test for corrosion resistance of stainless 
steel surgical instruments '. 

6.4 Subject to agreement between the purchaser and the suppUer the instrument may be put to the 
following tests: 

Copper sulpliate test — Scrub the sample with soap and warm water, rinse in hot water and 
then dip in 95 percent ethyl alcohol. Dry the sample. Immerse in copper sulphate solution at room 
temperature for 6 minutes and wash off with fresh water or wet cotton wool. Composition of the 
solution shall be as follows: 

Copper sulphate ( CuS04.5H,0 ) 4*0 g 

Sulphuric acid ( H.SO4 ) ( sp gr 1'84 ) lO'O g 

Distilled water [ see IS : 1070-1960 Specification for 
water, distilled quality {revised)] 90'0 ml 

No red stains or spots on the sample shall be allowed but dulling of the polished surface may 
be permitted. 

7. Marking — The curette shall be marked with the following: 

a) Manufacturer's name, initials or recognised trade-mar"R;; and 

b) The words ' Stainless Steel ' or letters * 55 

7.1 ISI Certification MarA/ng — Details available with the Indian Standards Institution. 

8. Packing — The curette shall be wrapped in moisture-proof paper or packed in polyethylene bags 
avoiding contact with one another. The curette may also be packed as agreed to between the 
purchaser and the supplier.
